notes: No `envelope`: the area is most of what an advisory is for, so the client returns the whole feature, as `zones.get_zone` does.
The OpenAPI also offers `application/vnd.noaa.uswx+xml` here. This client asks for GeoJSON only.

An advisory that does not exist answers 500 `UnexpectedProblem`, not 404 (measured 2026-09-30, `/aviation/cwsus/ZSE/cwas/2026-09-28/999`). So do most that do exist: on 2026-10-11, 206 of the 221 advisories `aviation.list_cwas` listed across eight units answered 500 at their own URL, and on 2026-10-12, 221 of 223, every one issued since 2026-10-06. The advisory is not gone: `aviation.list_cwas` still lists it, with its text and area. A 500 here does not mean the advisory does not exist, and asking again does not help; read it from the list instead. `refresh_examples.py` re-records the newest advisory that answers, and fails when none does.

spec.description: One Center Weather Advisory, with its area. Since 2026-10-06 the service has answered HTTP 500 for most advisories, including ones `aviation.list_cwas` lists; that list holds the same advisories, text and area included. A unit occasionally gives two advisories one sequence number on one day (measured 2026-09-30, `ZAB` issued two `206`s), and the service then answers one of them; `aviation.list_cwas` holds both.

request.title: GetCwaRequest
request.description: Which advisory: its unit, its issue date and its sequence number, as they end its URL.

cwsu_id.description: The unit, such as `ZSE` for Seattle Center.

date.description: UTC date the advisory was issued.

sequence.description: Sequence number, from 101 up: `properties.sequence` of the advisory.
